title: Circulating osteocrin is associated with cardiac remodeling in canine myxomatous mitral valve disease and skeletal alterations in a rat pressure-overload model.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) is the most common acquired cardiac disease in dogs and is increasingly recognized as a systemic disorder associated with extracardiac remodeling. Osteocrin (OSTN), a secreted peptide implicated in natriuretic peptide biology and skeletal homeostasis, has emerged as a potential candidate biomarker of cardiovascular-skeletal interactions. However, circulating OSTN dynamics during cardiovascular disease progression remain incompletely characterized.

METHODS: We employed a translational study design integrating a clinical cohort of dogs with naturally occurring myxomatous mitral valve disease (MMVD) and an experimental rat pressure-overload remodeling model. Circulating OSTN concentrations were evaluated alongside cardiac biomarkers, echocardiographic indices, bone mineral density, skeletal mechanical properties, and tissue localization by immunohistochemistry.

RESULTS: In the canine cohort (n = 47), circulating OSTN concentrations demonstrated stage-dependent alterations and were significantly associated with echocardiographic indices of cardiac remodeling. In the rat pressure-overload model, circulating OSTN concentrations increased, whereas NT-proBNP did not show a significant pressure-overload-associated increase. In pooled analyses, circulating OSTN was inversely associated with bone mineral density and stiffness; however, these associations were substantially influenced by between-group separation, whereas no significant associations were observed between NT-proBNP and the skeletal parameters examined. Multivariable regression analysis demonstrated that ACVIM disease stage remained significantly associated with circulating OSTN concentrations after adjustment for age and body weight.

CONCLUSION: Circulating OSTN was associated with cardiac remodeling in dogs with MMVD and with skeletal alterations in an experimental rat pressure-overload model. These findings support further investigation of OSTN as a candidate biomarker at the interface between cardiovascular and skeletal remodeling.
